::: {.callout-warning}

**You should install and set everything here _before_ the first day of class.**

:::

## Install the core class software

1. **Sign up for [Slack]({{< var slack >}})**. You should have been sent a link to join in the course intro email. If not, email Professor Helveston for an invite link. I recommend using your `@gwu.edu` email to sign up, but if you use another email for another Slack then use that.

2. **Install the Slack app** on your phone and **Turn notifications on!**. I'll send all course communication via Slack, so please make sure your notifications are on so you don't miss anything.

3. **Install Positron**, the code editor we'll use all semester: [download it here](https://positron.posit.co/download.html) and follow the install instructions for your OS. Positron is a free editor from Posit (the company behind RStudio), and it's where we'll work with Python, Quarto, and Claude Code together in one place.

4. [**Download and install Quarto**](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/). We'll use Quarto to build websites, documents, and slides.

5. **Install uv**, the tool we'll use to install and run Python. Open Positron, choose `Terminal > New Terminal` from the menu bar, then paste the line for your computer into the terminal and press Enter.

    **macOS**

    ```bash
    curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
    ```

    **Windows**

    ```powershell
    powershell -ExecutionPolicy ByPass -c "irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex"
    ```

    Then close that terminal (the trash icon on the terminal panel), open a new one, and run `uv python install` to install Python. If you see `command not found`, opening a fresh terminal is usually the fix. See the [uv docs](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) if you get stuck.

6. [**Download and install GitHub Desktop**](https://desktop.github.com/download/). All of our Git work in this class happens in GitHub Desktop, not the terminal.

7. **Create your GitHub account**: If you do not yet have a GitHub account, you'll need to [create one](https://github.com/signup?). Choose a user name that you like, recognizing that this will be viewed by many in the professional world (Professor Helveston's is [jhelvy](https://github.com/jhelvy/)), and use a personal email address that will follow you after leaving GW (I recommend **not** using your GW email as it eventually expires). Then open GitHub Desktop and sign in with that account.

## Install an agentic CLI tool

We start using AI coding agents in Week 3, so you'll need one installed. I will use and teach Claude Code in class as the primary agentic tool I recommend, though you are welcome to use an [alternative](#alternatives-to-claude-code) such as Google Gemini CLI.

### Installing Claude Code

You install Claude Code from inside Positron. Work through these five steps before the first day of class. You will need macOS 13 or newer, or Windows 10 or newer.

::: {.callout-tip}

Below are my suggested installation steps. If you have any difficulty, look over Anthropic's [Quickstart guide](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/quickstart). If you're still stuck, we can sort it out with you before or after class.

:::

#### Step 1: Get a Claude subscription

If you do not already have one, sign up now (but [check Slack first](syllabus.qmd#ai-tools-and-cost) in case we have institutional access). You'll need at least a [Claude Pro](https://claude.ai/login?plan=pro) subscription to use Claude Code -- a free account isn't sufficient.

#### Step 2: Open a terminal inside Positron

Open Positron, then from the menu bar, choose `Terminal > New Terminal`. A panel opens along the bottom of the window. Everything below happens in that panel, so you never need to leave Positron.

#### Step 3: Run the installer

Paste the line for your computer into the terminal, then press Enter.

**macOS**

```bash
curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash
```

**Windows**

```powershell
irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1 | iex
```

#### Step 4: Close that terminal, then open a new one

Use the trash icon on the terminal panel, then `Terminal > New Terminal` again. This step matters: the installer teaches your computer where `claude` lives, and only a freshly opened terminal knows about it.

To check that it worked, type `claude --version` and press Enter. You should see a version number such as `2.1.211 (Claude Code)`. If you instead see `command not found`, opening a new terminal is what fixes it nine times out of ten.

#### Step 5: Log in

Type `claude` and press Enter. A browser window opens: sign in with the Claude account you paid for in step 1. You only do this once.

## Alternatives to Claude Code

Claude Code is not the only agent that works this way. Both of these below run in Positron's terminal exactly like Claude Code does, and **Gemini CLI is free** with an ordinary Google account, though you can quickly run out of tokens using the free tier. The underlying skills we will cover (directing an agent, verifying its output) transfer. Just know that in-class instruction, troubleshooting help, and these materials will all assume Claude Code, so you're on your own for translating anything tool-specific.

- [**Gemini CLI**](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli): Google's coding agent for the terminal. The closest free stand-in for Claude Code, and the one to pick if you would rather not pay. *Free with a Google account.*

- [**Codex**](https://github.com/openai/codex): OpenAI's coding agent for the terminal. A good fit if you already pay for ChatGPT and want to stay in that account. *Needs a paid ChatGPT plan.*

## Set up later in the semester

You don't need these before the first class. We'll set them up together when we get to them.

- **A Gemini API key (Week 7).** We'll use it to have your agent generate images with Google's image model (Nano Banana). It's paid per image (see [AI Tools and Cost](syllabus.qmd#ai-tools-and-cost)). We'll also cover how to keep the key secret: it never goes in your code or in a commit.
- **Python packages.** Each build has its own project folder, and your agent installs the packages that project needs with `uv add` (for example, Pillow for images or plotnine for charts). You don't need to install them ahead of time.
- **Quarto with Python.** When a Quarto document runs Python code, the project needs `ipykernel` installed, and Quarto has to use that project's Python. The simplest way is to run Quarto through uv:

    ```bash
    uv add ipykernel
    uv run quarto render
    ```

    We write Python in `.py` scripts and `.qmd` files. **We don't use Jupyter notebooks (`.ipynb`) in this course.**

That's it - you're all set for class!
